transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-27 14:00 UTC | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Ethan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Sara Kim (Verdant Head of ML), Marcus Lee (Verdant Platform), Anita Desai (Verdant Procurement)

Summary:
Short renewal check-in to confirm capacity upgrade request (two additional dedicated GPUs), add EU region for serving, and discuss contract extension and pricing. Customer wants approximate costs and SOC2/KMS compliance details before moving forward.

Topics covered:
- Current usage and peak token throughput
- Dedicated vs. hosted for EU region
- Contract length discounts (12 vs 24 months)
- Security/compliance (SOC2, KMS, VPC)
- Next steps: revised quote, benchmark, security docs

Transcript:
00:00 Ethan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check-in today, just want to run through Verdant's renewal window and the expansion asks you sent last week. Sara, do you want to kick off with current usage?
00:18 Sara (Verdant): Yeah thanks Ethan. So we're seeing pretty steady growth, current prod uses about 120k tokens/day, peaks at ~2.5k rps in batch at midday, um, and the current dedicated pool is kind of pegged. We want to add two more GPUs to avoid queueing during spikes — especially with the new recommendations feature rolling out.
00:35 Marcus (Verdant): To add, our infra team wants an EU region so latency for EU customers is sub 80ms. Right now routing to US causes 150-200ms which is not ideal.
00:50 Priya (Redwood SE): Got it. Two more GPUs and a new EU region. A couple quick clarifying q's — are you planning to replicate data in EU, or just serve inference from EU but keep data in US? That affects KMS / data residency conversation.
01:07 Sara: We prefer to keep data residency in the US for now, but inference in EU is acceptable. We might revisit residency later.
01:15 Ethan: OK — that makes routing simpler. We can add region for serving only, we'll surface the EU region pricing. For dedicated capacity, we have two options: reserve additional GPUs on your existing Dedicated pool, or we can create a separate EU-dedicated pool. Separate pool gives stronger isolation but costs a bit more.
01:36 Marcus: What's the numbers ballpark? We need a calc for ops to justify the spend.
01:44 Priya: Roughly, adding 2x A100-equivalent GPUs to an existing pool is about +$Xk/month; separate EU-dedicated pool with same size is closer to +$Yk/month because of regional infra premiums. I'll put exacts in the revised quote. Also note that we can do bursting in the EU region to shared capacity for non-SLA-critical traffic to save cost.
02:05 Anita (Procurement): On contract length — Verdant's procurement prefers 24 months but we need to see a discount matrix. Can you provide 12 vs 24 month pricing and any commit tiers?
02:18 Ethan: Absolutely. Standard renewal options are 12 or 24 months; we can provide tiered discounts at the 3 GPU, 6 GPU, and 12 GPU committed levels. I'll include a comparison table. For 24 months we can give an extra 7-10% depending on commit.
02:34 Sara: Also need to confirm SOC2 and KMS. We run PCI-like workloads and need to show our auditors Redwood's controls — network diagrams, where keys live, rotation policy.
02:45 Priya: We're SOC 2 Type II certified — I'll share the SOC attestation and the network diagram. Regarding KMS, we support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own KMS) and HSM integrations in Private deployments; for Dedicated customers we do KMS integration via our key wrap flow. If you want, Marcus and I can map out key lifecycle.
03:05 Marcus: That would be helpful. We also need to know about audit logs retention — we keep logs for 2 years internally, want to ensure Redwood's logs can be exported or held for 12 months at least.
03:17 Ethan: Yes, log export's supported — we'll include the retention options and pricing for longer log retention in the doc.
03:25 Anita: Procurement timeline — we're aiming to sign before end of April to line up with budget cycles. Can you commit to that?
03:33 Ethan: We can aim for that. I'll get the quote by Apr 1 and Priya will run benchmarks the week after so you have perf numbers.
03:40 Priya: On benchmarks — to make them meaningful please send your typical prompt mix, average sequence lengths, and expected concurrency. Marcus, can you share the infra diagrams and expected peak qps?
03:50 Marcus: Yep I can send that today.
03:53 Ethan: Great. Any concerns about vendor lock-in or model compatibility?
03:57 Sara: We're evaluating Anthropic for some workloads but Redwood's batching and cost controls are attractive. Need to see unit cost delta though.
04:06 Ethan: Totally — we'll include per-token cost comparisons in the quote and highlight where intelligent batching/caching reduces effective unit cost.
04:15 (short crosstalk)
04:20 Priya: A technical note: if you do EU-serving-only (no data residency), we'll need to validate network egress and latency. For the test harness I'll configure a small set of EU endpoints so we can measure 95th percentile tail.
04:35 Marcus: Sounds good. Also curious about model variants fallback — if EU capacity saturated, can Redwood auto-fallback to US region? We want graceful degradation, not timeouts.
04:45 Priya: Yes, smart routing policies can fallback to US or to hosted model variants with lower capacity. We can set SLO-based fallback rules. I'll demo that in the benchmark session.
04:58 Anita: For procurement I need a clean summary sheet with the ask, cost delta, approval path, and PO instructions.
05:07 Ethan: I'll prepare that and include both 12- and 24-month options and the discount matrix.
05:12 Sara: One last question — can we get committed throughput guarantees on the Dedicated pool? We want SLOs for token latency and availability.
05:20 Ethan: Yes, Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; I'll pull the SLA doc and include the latency targets for your config.
05:28 (someone shares link) Ethan: Shared: Renewal deck link (https://redwood.example/renewal-deck/VDT) and security pack (https://redwood.example/security/VDT-pack).
05:40 Priya: I'll follow up with the benchmark plan doc and a proposed test matrix.
05:46 Recap (final 2 min):
Ethan: To recap — Verdant requests +2 GPUs, EU serving region (no data residency initially), interest in 24-month contract if discount math works. Action items: Ethan update quote (12/24 mo + EU pricing), Priya to prepare benchmark plan and run with Marcus, Marcus to send infra diagram + qps, Anita to confirm procurement timeline. We'll aim to have the quote by 2026-04-01 and the benchmark week of 2026-04-06.
46:00 Sara: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
